message.content:
The largest planet that astronomers have confirmed so far is the gas giant **HD 100546 b**. It orbits the young B-type star HD 100546 at a distance of roughly 10–15 astronomical units (AU). Its size is enormous – its radius is about **2.5 times that of Jupiter**, making it one of the most inflated planets ever found. In terms of mass, estimates place it between **20 and 30 Jupiter masses** (roughly 0.02–0.03 solar masses), which is close to the deuterium‑burning limit that separates massive planets from brown dwarfs. 

Because exoplanet discoveries are constantly being refined, future observations may reveal even larger planets or clarify whether HD 100546 b is truly the biggest. For now, though, it holds the record among confirmed exoplanets.
